text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

Thanks for reaching out — I'm glad to help the three of you sort this out. Before we look at any plan, I'd like to understand what matters to each of you. Could you tell me a bit more from your side: what is it about having the trailer in the next few weeks that matters to you? Is there a specific project or event, or something else underneath the timing? No wrong answers — I just want to understand the need, not the schedule yet.
I need it for a project at my house, and it needs to happen in the next few weeks. I’m not willing to just wait until A is done with it.

Hi — C contacted me to help the three of you figure out how to share the trailer you bought together. I'd like to hear from you too. What matters most to you about how the trailer gets used and stored? Take your time — I want to understand what you need before anyone talks solutions.
I want to be able to use it for my weekend trips in the next few weeks. I don’t have a strong view on where it’s stored.

Hi — C contacted me to help the three of you figure out how to share the trailer you bought together, and I understand you're kind of in the middle since it's parked at your place. What matters most to you about the arrangement? Any concerns, even small ones, are welcome. I want to understand what you need before anyone talks solutions.

I’d like it not to take up space on my pad much longer, though it’s fine for now. I did agree to keep it here, so I feel a bit bad asking—but I rent, and I’d need my landlord’s permission to change what’s kept there. I haven’t asked him yet.

Thanks. Let me check I've got your need right. You have a project at your house with a timeline, and what matters to you is being able to get that project done when it needs to get done. Does that capture it? If it's off, tell me how you'd say it.
Not quite. It’s not just the project timeline—I need to be able to use the trailer myself, rather than have my plans depend on when A is finished.

Thank you for the correction. How about this: what matters to you is being able to make your own plans and carry them out without them depending on someone else's schedule. Does that fit? If not, how would you say it?
Yes. I need the freedom to make my own plans with the trailer, and I need to use it in the next few weeks.
Thanks, A. Let me check I've got your need right: what matters to you is being able to take your weekend trips when you want to take them. Does that capture it? If it's off, tell me how you'd say it.
Mostly. I want the freedom to take it on my trips without having to negotiate every single time.

Thanks, B. Let me check I've got your need right — and please know there's nothing to feel bad about; raising this is helpful, not a burden. Would it fit to say: what matters to you is that whatever is stored at your place has your landlord's OK, so your housing isn't put at risk? Does that capture it, or how would you say it?
Not quite—I do want to be sure I’m allowed to keep it there, but mostly I’d like the trailer out of the way. I just feel a little awkward asking, since I agreed to the arrangement.

That's really helpful, and thank you for being honest even though it feels awkward — your agreement to store it was a favor, not a permanent commitment, and it's completely fair to revisit it. Would this capture it: what matters to you is having your space back — not having the trailer take up room on your pad — and knowing whatever is kept there is allowed by your landlord? If not quite, how would you say it?
Yes, that’s closer. I’d like the pad back, and I should check with my landlord before agreeing to keep it there longer. I still feel a little responsible since I agreed to it.

Here's where we stand, and a draft to react to. The needs on the list so far: (C) freedom to make your own plans with the trailer, and use it in the next few weeks; (A) freedom to take it on trips without negotiating every single time; (B) getting the pad back, and checking with your landlord before agreeing to store it longer. One of my own, as a fellow participant: I'd like whatever we choose to keep the neighbor relationships good — nobody left feeling blamed. Draft options: (1) Relocate the trailer during the next few weeks — e.g., park it at C's during his project and at A's place on his trip weekends — then find a non-B storage spot after. (2) Move it to rented or alternative storage now, so B's pad is freed and both of you can come and go without going through B. (3) A fixed calendar with alternating blocks. My worry with (3) is it means negotiating less freely, so it may not meet C's and A's needs. Would any of these work for you — and does anyone have even a minor discomfort with any of them? A no is useful information, not a problem.

Option 2 sounds best to me if the storage is affordable and we can all access the trailer. I’m uncomfortable committing before we know the cost and availability. A fixed calendar doesn’t work for me; I don’t want to negotiate every trip.
